title: The universities
hook: Paris grew from its cathedral school; Oxford and Bologna rose in the same age

segments.voice: Yesterday, Dominic, who sold his books for the hungry and then sent his friars to study. Your line was to contemplate and to share.

An open book on a coat of arms, the arms of the University of Oxford, and written across its pages, Dominus illuminatio mea. The words open a psalm, in the Douay-Rheims: "The Lord is my light and my salvation, whom shall I fear?" A place famous for lectures and libraries and examinations chose, for its badge, a line of prayer. It's a clue to where the whole idea of a university came from.
screen: `DOMINUS ILLUMINATIO MEA.` → `A PSALM ON AN OPEN BOOK.` → `A CLUE TO WHERE IT CAME FROM.`

segments.voice: In the middle ages, bishops kept schools at their cathedrals to train clergy to read, to sing the liturgy and to understand scripture. In Paris, the school by the cathedral of Notre-Dame drew teachers, and the teachers drew students, until the streets around were full of both. In the cities, bakers and masons banded together into guilds to protect their trade. Teachers and students did the same. In Latin, such a sworn body could be called a universitas, a whole company of people bound together. The masters of Paris, the students of Bologna and the scholars of Oxford organized this way, and won rights from popes and kings to govern themselves. A day there was built on two things. The lecture: a master read a text aloud, line by line, and explained it. And the disputation: a question was posed, the arguments against were stated fairly, then the master gave his answer and replied to each objection. Some readers see Anselm's phrase from day eight hundred, faith seeking understanding, turned here into a daily routine. You didn't win by shouting. You had to state the other side fairly before you answered it. Degrees, the lecture hall, the idea that a question deserves an argument: these grew in schools where theology was taught alongside law and medicine and the arts. The friars from yesterday's story went to these towns to study and teach. Learning was treated as a way of loving God with the mind.
screen: `THE SCHOOL BY THE CATHEDRAL.` · `A GUILD OF MASTERS AND STUDENTS.` · `LECTURE, THEN DISPUTATION.` · `FAITH SEEKING UNDERSTANDING.` · then, large: `THE LORD IS MY LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Pick a hard question you've been avoiding, in your faith, your work or your life, and do what a disputation does: state the strongest case against your own view as fairly as you can, then let your answer come and see whether it meets the objection. There's no need to finish. If you pray, begin with the psalm's line, the Lord is my light.
University. The universitas: a sworn company of masters and students, growing in cities like Paris from the schools beside the cathedrals. Today's word.
Your line: faith builds schools. The week ran from the stones of San Damiano to the lecture hall. That's day eight hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Catholic universities today, and the Church's own pontifical faculties, keep the medieval pairing of faith and study; Catholics speak of theology as faith seeking understanding.

notes: The index hook says Paris, Oxford and Bologna all grew from cathedral schools; Bologna grew mainly from student and law associations, so the hook line here was adjusted and the voice ties only Paris to its cathedral school. Owner may want the index hook updated.
Oxford's motto 'Dominus illuminatio mea' (Vulgate Psalm 26:1) on its arms with an open book: confirm.
'Three Latin words': counted from the motto. Psalm 26:1 Douay-Rheims wording: confirm.

Universitas as a guild/corporation and the 'masters of Paris, students of Bologna' contrast: history claims; confirm. The original game gives the Latin meaning; it is a definition, not a derivation, but flag per the claims rule.
Lecture and disputation described generally; Anselm's 'fides quaerens intellectum' (Proslogion's original title) paraphrased. Confirm.
'Degrees, gowns, the lecture hall' as medieval inheritances: confirm or soften.
